extracted.intended_audience: parties, attorneys, and carriers participating in FCC complaint proceedings (47 CFR Part 1)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for filing, responding to, and litigating informal and formal complaints before the Federal Communications Commission under 47 CFR Part 1, Subpart E.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show cause order content
rubrics_metrics.description: The order shall contain a statement of the particulars and matters concerning which the Commission is inquiring and the reasons for such action, and will call upon the carrier to appear before the Commission at a place and time therein stated and give evidence upon the matters specified in the order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission may commence proceedings by serving such an order; carrier must respond as specified in the order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show cause answer requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Any carrier upon whom an order has been served shall file its answer within the time specified in the order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer must specifically and completely respond to all allegations and matters contained in the show cause order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformity of papers in show cause proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: All papers filed by a carrier in a proceeding under this section shall conform with the specifications of §§ 1.49 and 1.50 and the subscription and verification requirements of § 1.52.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See those sections for formatting, signature, and verification rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appearance at hearings (no advance filing required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as otherwise required by specific rules, no written statement indicating intent to appear need be filed in advance of actual appearance at any hearing by any person or his attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: §1.221 (application proceedings), §1.91 (section 312 proceedings), or by Commission order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral argument appearance filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 5 days after release of an order designating an initial decision for oral argument (or other time specified), any party who wishes to participate must file a written statement indicating they will appear and participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For other matters designated for oral argument, a written statement setting forth reasons for interest is required; the Commission will advise whether participation is permitted. See §1.277 for penalties for failure to file appearance statements in certain proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission counsel exception for appearance statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement to file appearance statements for oral arguments does not apply to counsel representing the Commission or the Chief of the Enforcement Bureau.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal complaint form contents (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: An informal complaint shall be in writing and should contain: (a) name, address and telephone number of the complainant; (b) name of the carrier; (c) complete statement of facts showing contravention of the Communications Act; and (d) specific relief sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for complaints under section 208; see §1.716 for detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal complaint processing procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission will forward informal complaints to the appropriate carrier for investigation and may set a due date for the carrier to provide a written response to the informal complaint to the Commission, with a copy to the complainant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If carrier's response or communications indicate the complaint has been satisfied, Commission may close the proceeding; otherwise notify complainant that a formal complaint may be filed if unsatisfied or if carrier fails to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal complaint relates back to informal complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: When an informal complaint has not been satisfied, a formal complaint filed in the form specified in §1.721 will be deemed to relate back to the filing date of the informal complaint provided the formal complaint is filed within 6 months from the date of the carrier's response (or due date if no response), references the informal complaint date, and is based on the same cause of action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no formal complaint filed within 6 months, informal complaint proceeding will be closed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 258 (slamming) informal complaint form
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaints alleging unauthorized change of a subscriber's preferred carrier shall be in writing and should contain: complainant contact info including e-mail (if any); names of both allegedly unauthorized and authorized carriers; complete statement of facts with documentation; whether complainant paid disputed charges; and specific relief sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures notwithstanding §§1.716–1.718; special timing and content rules apply under §1.719.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 258 complaint procedure and remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will resolve slamming complaints under the definitions and procedures in §§64.1100–64.1190 and will issue a written/electronic order informing complainant and carriers of its finding and ordering appropriate remedy as defined in §§64.1160–64.1170.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 258 relation-back special timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal complaints relating back to an informal section 258 complaint must be filed within 45 days from the date an order resolving the informal complaint is mailed/electronically delivered, reference the informal complaint number and initial filing date, and be based on the same cause of action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no formal complaint filed within 45 days, complainant is deemed to have abandoned right to bring formal complaint on that cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of formal complaint rules (§1.720 purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: These procedural rules apply to formal complaint proceedings under 47 U.S.C. 208, pole attachment complaints under 47 U.S.C. 224, and advanced communications services/equipment formal complaints under specified statutes and part 14; additional subpart J rules apply to pole attachment complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pleadings resolved on written record
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal complaint proceedings are generally resolved on a written record consisting of complaint, answer, reply, and joint statement of stipulated facts, disputed facts and key legal issues, along with associated evidence; Commission may require/permit briefs, proposed findings, other submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission has discretion to request additional written submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformity to general filing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All papers filed must be drawn in conformity with the requirements of §§1.49, 1.50, and 1.52.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Those sections govern form, filing, signatures, and verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pleadings must be clear, concise, direct
rubrics_metrics.description: Pleadings must be clear, concise, and direct. All matters concerning a claim, defense or requested remedy, including damages, should be pleaded fully and with specificity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad admonition: specificity required for claims and remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plead facts sufficient to state violation or defense
rubrics_metrics.description: Pleadings must contain facts which, if true, are sufficient to constitute a violation of the Act or a Commission regulation or order, or a defense to an alleged violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbered paragraphs and single-issue paragraphs
rubrics_metrics.description: Averred facts, claims, or defenses shall be made in numbered paragraphs and must be supported by relevant evidence. Each paragraph should be limited as far as practicable to a statement of a single set of circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each claim from a separate transaction/occurrence and each affirmative defense should be separately stated to facilitate clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on assertions based on information and belief
rubrics_metrics.description: Assertions based on information and belief are prohibited unless made in good faith and accompanied by a declaration or affidavit explaining basis for belief and why facts could not reasonably be ascertained from other sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal arguments must be supported by authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal arguments must be supported by appropriate statutory, judicial, or administrative authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish opposing authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Opposing authorities must be distinguished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If relying on contrary authority, explain why it does not control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide copies of non-routine authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies must be provided of all non-Commission authorities relied upon which are not routinely available in national reporting systems (e.g., unpublished decisions or slip opinions). Copies of state authorities relied upon shall be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing accuracy and updating of submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties are responsible for continuing accuracy and completeness of all information and supporting authority furnished in a pending complaint; information and relevant legal authorities must be current and updated as necessary and in a timely manner before decision on merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific reference to tariffs or contracts and appendices
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific reference shall be made to any tariff or contract provision relied upon; copies of relevant tariffs, contracts, or relevant portions referred to or relied upon shall be appended to the pleading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify contact information for filer/attorney
rubrics_metrics.description: Pleadings shall identify the name, address, telephone number, and email address for either the filing party's attorney or, where not represented, the filing party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pleadings may be signed by an attorney.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachments must be Bates-stamped and cited
rubrics_metrics.description: All attachments shall be Bates-stamped or otherwise numbered sequentially. Parties shall cite to Bates-stamped page numbers in their pleadings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and certificate of service requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Pleadings shall be served on all parties in accordance with §1.734 and shall include a certificate of service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification and signature certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Each pleading or other submission must contain a written verification that the signatory has read the submission and, after reasonable inquiry, it is well grounded in fact and warranted by existing law or a good faith argument to change law; not interposed for improper purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If signed in violation, Commission may impose sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver petition for rules governing formal complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may petition staff, pursuant to §1.3, for a waiver of any rules governing formal complaints; waiver may be granted for good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to dismissal without prejudice before final action
rubrics_metrics.description: A complaint may, on request of the filing party, be dismissed without prejudice as a matter of right prior to the adoption date of any final action taken by the Commission with respect to the complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request for return of an initiating document will be regarded as request for dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on amendments adding new claims or requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments or supplements to complaints to add new claims or requests for relief are prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to prosecute leads to dismissal
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to prosecute a complaint will be cause for dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaints must state a cause of action
rubrics_metrics.description: Any document purporting to be a formal complaint which does not state a cause of action under the Communications Act or a Commission regulation or order will be dismissed; amendment/supplement considered a new filing subject to statutory limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defective pleadings may be struck or corrected
rubrics_metrics.description: Any other pleading that does not conform with requirements may be deemed defective; Commission may strike the pleading or request corrections and proper pleadings within a prescribed time to be part of the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pleadings construed to do justice
rubrics_metrics.description: Pleadings shall be construed so as to do justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions for failure to respond to Commission directives
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party that fails to respond to official correspondence, a request for additional information, or an order or directive from the Commission may be subject to appropriate sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal complaint required contents (names of parties)
rubrics_metrics.description: A formal complaint shall contain the name of each complainant and defendant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal complaint required contents (occupation/address/phone)
rubrics_metrics.description: A formal complaint shall contain the occupation, address and telephone number of each complainant and, to the extent known, each defendant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal complaint required contents (attorney contact)
rubrics_metrics.description: If represented by counsel, the complaint must include the name, address, telephone number, and email address of complainant's attorney.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal complaint required contents (citation to law/regulation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaint must cite the section of the Communications Act or Commission regulation or order alleged to have been violated; each alleged violation shall be stated in a separate count.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal complaint required contents (legal analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaint must include legal analysis relevant to the claims and arguments set forth therein.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal complaint required contents (relief sought & damages)
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaint must state the relief sought, including recovery of damages and the amount of damages claimed, if known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal complaint required certification of settlement efforts
rubrics_metrics.description: Certification that the complainant has, in good faith, discussed or attempted to discuss possibility of settlement with each defendant prior to filing; for business disputes must include executive-level discussions; must include that complainant notified defendant in writing of allegations and invited response within reasonable time and a brief summary of additional steps taken to resolve dispute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refusal by defendant to engage in such discussions may constitute an unreasonable practice under the Act. §1.722(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal complaint required statement of related actions
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement explaining whether a separate action has been filed with the Commission, any court, or other government agency based on same claim or facts, or whether complaint seeks prospective relief identical to relief in a concurrent notice-and-comment rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal complaint information designation (people & subjects)
rubrics_metrics.description: An information designation containing: (1) name and, if known, address and telephone number of each individual likely to have information relevant to proceeding, along with subjects of that information, excluding individuals otherwise identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal complaint information designation (documents)
rubrics_metrics.description: An information designation containing: (2) a copy—or a description by category and location—of all relevant documents, ESI, and tangible things in possession, custody, or control, excluding documents submitted with the complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal complaint intake form required
rubrics_metrics.description: A completed Formal Complaint Intake Form must be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing fee declaration and FRN requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A declaration, under penalty of perjury, describing amount, method, and date of payment of filing fee required under §1.1106 and the complainant's 10-digit FCC Registration Number; submission without FRN will result in dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear, unequivocal request for damages
rubrics_metrics.description: If a complainant wishes to recover damages, the complaint must contain a clear and unequivocal request for damages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damages computation or explanation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: When recovery of damages is sought, complaint must include either (1) a computation of each and every category of damages with identification of relevant documents/evidence to prove amounts, or (2) if information not in possession is necessary, an explanation of why unavailable, factual basis for belief such evidence exists, and a detailed outline of methodology to compute damages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Option to bifurcate damages proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: Complainant may request damages determination in a separate proceeding subsequent to liability/prospective relief, but must comply with paragraph (a) and state clearly the desire for separate damages proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental complaint for damages relates back
rubrics_metrics.description: When separate damages proceeding is used, complainant may initiate it by filing a supplemental complaint within 60 days after public notice of a decision with finding of liability; supplemental complaints need not comply with certain earlier requirements and will relate back for statutory limitations purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission may require bond/escrow for likely damages
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission may order defendant to post bond or deposit into escrow a sum equal to likely damages upon preliminary investigation, provided Commission, considering listed factors, finds such relief favored on balance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors: (1) complainant's potential irreparable injury; (2) extent damages can be accurately calculated; (3) balance of hardships; (4) public interest considerations. §1.723(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission may adopt damages computation method
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission may end adjudication of damages by adopting a damages computation method or formula; parties must negotiate in good faith to agree amount pursuant to method and within 30 days submit joint statement detailing agreement, continuing negotiations, or bases for dispute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission may suspend damages proceedings for settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: In any proceeding without statutory deadline, Commission may suspend ongoing damages proceedings to provide time for settlement negotiations or mediation under §1.737.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-complaint procedures for 47 U.S.C. 208(b)(1) 5-month deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party intending to file a complaint subject to the 5-month deadline must comply with pre-complaint procedures; Enforcement Bureau's Market Disputes Resolution Division will not process such complaints unless filer complies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and conference for 5-month deadline complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: A party seeking to file such complaint shall notify the Chief of the Market Disputes Resolution Division in writing of intent and provide copy to defendant; staff will convene a conference with both parties to discuss scheduling, narrowing issues, information exchange/discovery, protective orders, and mandatory settlement negotiation preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-complaint information exchange
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff will endeavor to complete the pre-complaint process expeditiously and may direct parties to exchange relevant information during the pre-complaint period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joinder of complainants and causes of action
rubrics_metrics.description: Two or more complainants may join in one complaint if their causes of action are against the same defendant and concern substantially the same facts and alleged violation; two or more grounds of complaint involving substantially the same facts may be included in one complaint but should be separately stated and numbered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer timing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Any defendant served with a formal complaint shall answer within 30 calendar days of service unless otherwise directed by the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer content and specificity requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Answer shall advise complainant and Commission fully of nature of any defense and respond specifically to all material allegations; defendant shall attempt to narrow issues, state concise defenses, admit or deny averments, and state basis for admissions/denials; general denials prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denials based on information and belief prohibited unless accompanied by declaration explaining basis and why facts could not reasonably be ascertained; if defendant lacks knowledge it shall so state which has effect of denial; partial denials must specify true portion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer must include legal analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The answer shall include legal analysis relevant to the claims and arguments set forth therein.

rubrics_metrics.name: Averments deemed admitted if not denied
rubrics_metrics.description: Averments in a complaint or supplemental complaint are deemed admitted when not denied in the answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affirmative defenses must be captioned
rubrics_metrics.description: Affirmative defenses to allegations shall be specifically captioned as such and presented separately from denials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer information designation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The answer shall include an information designation containing names/contacts of individuals likely to have information and a copy/description of all relevant documents/ESI in possession, custody or control (excluding documents submitted with complaint/answer).

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to file answer consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to file an answer may be deemed an admission of the material facts alleged; defendant failing to file and serve an answer may be deemed in default and an order may be entered against defendant per complaint allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-complaints and counterclaims prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-complaints seeking any relief within Commission jurisdiction against any party to that proceeding are prohibited; any claim that might otherwise meet cross-complaint requirements may be filed as a separate complaint. For purposes of this subpart, 'cross-complaint' includes counterclaims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply timing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A complainant shall file and serve a reply within 10 calendar days of service of the answer, unless otherwise directed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply scope limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: The reply shall contain statements of relevant, material facts and legal arguments that respond to factual allegations and legal arguments made by the defendant. Other allegations or arguments will not be considered by the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to reply will not be deemed admission except with respect to affirmative defenses; failure to reply to an affirmative defense deemed an admission of that defense and supporting facts. §1.728(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply must include legal analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The reply shall include legal analysis relevant to the claims and arguments set forth therein.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply information designation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The reply shall include an information designation containing names/contacts of individuals likely to have information referenced in the reply and a copy/description of relevant documents/ESI/tangible things addressed in the reply (excluding documents submitted with complaint or answer).

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions must be written and particularized
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for a Commission order shall be by written motion, stating with particularity the grounds and authority therefor, including supporting legal analysis, and setting forth the relief sought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions to compel discovery certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Motions to compel discovery must contain a certification that a good faith attempt to resolve the dispute was made prior to filing the motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion for more definite statement prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: Motions seeking an order that the allegations in the complaint be made more definite and certain are prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to dismiss allowed but doesn't stay deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Motions to dismiss all or part of a complaint are permitted; filing such a motion does not suspend other filing deadlines unless staff issues an order suspending them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oppositions to motions timing and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Oppositions to motions shall be filed and served within 5 business days after the motion is served and shall be limited to issues and allegations contained in the motion; oppositions to motions incorporated in an answer shall not address issues outside those raised in the motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to oppose may be grounds for granting the motion. §1.729(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: No reply to opposition except by staff direction
rubrics_metrics.description: No reply may be filed to an opposition to a motion, except under direction of Commission staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interrogatory limits and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A complainant may serve up to 10 written interrogatories with complaint, defendant may serve up to 10 with answer, complainant may serve up to 5 additional with reply; subparts count separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interrogatories may seek any non-privileged matter relevant to material facts in dispute and may not be used for delay/harassment/overbroad inquiries. §1.730(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interrogatories must justify necessity
rubrics_metrics.description: Interrogatories must contain an explanation of why the information sought is necessary to resolution of the dispute and not available from any other source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objections to interrogatories timing and specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise directed, within seven calendar days, responding party shall file with the Commission and serve any opposition and objections to interrogatories; grounds for objection must be stated with specificity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any interrogatories with no timely objection shall be answered within 20 calendar days. §1.730(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission staff rulings on disputed interrogatories
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission staff shall rule in writing on scope and schedule for answering disputed interrogatories based on justification and any objections/oppositions properly filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interrogatory answers under oath and signature requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Interrogatories shall be answered separately and fully in writing under oath or affirmation by the party served, or by officer/agent for corporate parties, and answers signed by person making them; attorney who objects must sign objections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answers shall be filed with the Commission and served on the propounding party. §1.730(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission may authorize additional discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission, in its discretion, may allow additional discovery including document production and depositions and may modify scope, means and scheduling in light of case needs and statutory deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic production and indexing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission may require parties to provide documents in scanned/electronic format that indexes documents by useful identifying information and allows staff to annotate the index for efficient review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to compel discovery timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A propounding party asserting inadequate/insufficient response to discovery may file a motion to compel within ten days of service of such response, or as otherwise directed by staff, pursuant to §1.729 requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential designation burden and specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: Any information produced may be designated confidential by party believing in good faith it falls within FOIA exemptions; party asserting confidentiality must clearly mark each page/portion and restrict designations to only the specific information claimed confidential; burden to demonstrate nondisclosure under FOIA if challenged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public redacted version and machine readability
rubrics_metrics.description: File with Commission a public version that redacts confidential information and clearly marks each page with header 'Public Version'; redacted document shall be machine-readable whenever technically possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If metadata is confidential/privileged, filer may remove metadata before electronic filing. §1.731(a)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: File unredacted confidential hard copy with Secretary
rubrics_metrics.description: File with the Secretary's Office an unredacted hard copy clearly marked 'Confidential Version' on each page the same day as the redacted version is filed electronically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serve hard copies of redacted and unredacted materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Serve one hard copy of the unredacted materials and one hard copy of the redacted materials on the attorney of record for each party (or each unrepresented party) by hand, overnight, or email, with proof of service per §§1.47(g) and 1.734(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on disclosure of confidential materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Attorney of record or party receiving unredacted confidential materials may disclose solely to specified persons (support personnel, officers/employees directly involved, consultants/expert witnesses, court reporters) only for use in prosecuting or defending the case and only to extent necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must sign a declaration/affidavit stating they reviewed Commission's rules and understand limitations. §1.731(b)-(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Copying and copy-log requirements for confidential materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may make copies of confidential materials solely for use by Commission or persons designated; each party shall maintain a log recording number of copies and persons to whom copies provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protective orders and return/destruction of confidential material
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission may adopt protective orders with further restrictions; upon termination of proceeding (including appeals), parties shall ensure originals and reproductions of confidential materials and the log are provided to producing party and notes/work product derived from confidential materials are destroyed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission may require briefs summarizing claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission may require parties to file briefs summarizing facts and issues and presenting relevant legal authority; may limit scope of briefs and unless directed, briefs must include all claims and defenses previously set forth in pleadings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims/defenses not reflected in briefs will be deemed abandoned; Commission may require any additional information it deems appropriate. §1.732.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status conference authority
rubrics_metrics.description: In any complaint proceeding, the Commission may direct attorneys and/or parties to appear before it for a status conference.
